turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**Target range:** 225 → 1190 MPa. The strongest samples (target > 1000 MPa) form a very clear, consistent process/composition cluster.

**Process signature of the top ~30 rows (all ≥ 1000 MPa):**
- `NT = 930`, `THT = 30`, `THt = 0`, `THQCr = 0` — high normalizing, no through-hardening hold
- `CT = 930` (max austenitizing), `DT ≈ 850–895`, `Dt = 15–70`, `QmT = 60–140` — aggressive quench
- `TT = 160–200`, `Tt = 120`, `TCr = 0.5` — **low tempering temperature** (this is the single biggest lever; every high-strength row uses TT ≈ 160–200, while the 400–650 tempering rows top out ~600 MPa)

**Composition signature:** Low-to-moderate carbon (C ≈ 0.17–0.23), and strong hardenability from **either** high Ni (~1.6) **or** high Cr (~1.1), with Mo ≈ 0.15–0.21. Best rows: Ni=1.69/Cr=0.55 → 1190; Ni=0.06/Cr=1.17 → 1144.

**Robustness strategy:** Because both high-Ni and high-Cr independently produce the top plateau, I combine **moderate-high Ni AND moderate-high Cr plus Mo**. This puts the alloy well inside the fully-hardenable regime, so a ±5% wobble in any one hardenability element cannot drop the microstructure off the martensitic cliff. I keep TT centered at ~170 (safely inside the 160–200 high-strength band) rather than at an edge, and pick RedRatio ~600 (interior of the top-cluster spread, avoiding the sparse extremes at 240 and 5530).

This lands in a broad interior of the high-strength cluster rather than on a single sharp record-holder.

## Proposal
